title: Cap. 7 Scholastici: Aquinas — eternal ordination completed through Christ
pass_a_gloss: 2. Aquinas, part 3, question 24, article 4. God preordained our salvation, by predestining from eternity that it should be completed through Jesus Christ. Aquinas speaks of elect human beings, and asserts that God from eternity ordained that their salvation should be completed through Jesus Christ infallibly. I ask therefore how Christ would have shown himself conformed to this eternal ordination of his Father, if in his saving passion he did not apply his merits in a peculiar manner unto infallibly effecting and completing the elect's salvation? There must therefore be conceded a special intention of God accepting this victim, and of Christ offering himself, restricted to the elect alone, insofar as Christ's passion is joined with an infallible effect of salvation in singular persons.
pass_b_english: 2. Aquinas (ST III q.24 a.4): God preordained our salvation by eternally predestining that it be completed through Jesus Christ. He is speaking of the elect, and he holds that from eternity God ordained their salvation to be finished through Christ without fail. How then could Christ have matched that eternal ordination of his Father if, in his saving passion, he did not apply his merits in a peculiar way to effect and complete the elect's salvation without fail? So we must grant a special intention — God accepting this victim, Christ offering himself — restricted to the elect alone, so far as Christ's passion is joined to an infallible saving effect in particular persons.
source_text: 2. Aquinas, part. 3. qu. 24. art. 4. Deus praeordinavit nostram salutem, ab aeterno praedestinando ut per Jesum Christum compleretur. Loquitur Aquinas de hominibus electis, atque asserit Deum ab aeterno ordinasse, ut eorum salus per Jesum Christum infallibiliter compleretur. Quaero igitur quomodo Christus huic aeternae ordinationi Patris sui sese conformem exhibuerit, si in passione sua salutifera ad electorum salutem infallibiliter efficiendam & complendam merita sua peculiari modo non applicaverit? Concedenda est itaque specialis intentio Dei hanc hostiam acceptantis, & Christi seipsum offerentis, restricta ad solos electos, quatenus passio Christi cum infallibili effectu salutis in singularibus personis conjungitur.
